questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the alcohol obtained when aldehyde other than formaldehyde is treated with Grignard's reagent followed by hydrolysis.
questions.solution:
Formaldehyde reacts with Grignard reagent to form primary alcohols.

Aldehydes other than formaldehyde react with Grignard reagent to form secondary alcohols.

Ketones react with Grignard reagent to form tertiary alcohols.

The reaction of an aldehyde ($R'CHO$) with Grignard reagent ($RMgX$) proceeds as follows:

$R'CHO + RMgX \rightarrow R'-CH(OMgX)-R$

Hydrolysis of the intermediate adduct gives a secondary alcohol:

$R'-CH(OMgX)-R + H_2O \rightarrow R'-CH(OH)-R + Mg(OH)X$

Thus, a secondary alcohol is obtained.

Answer: Secondary alcohol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find the structure of A in following reaction
questions.solution:
The given reaction is the acid-catalyzed hydration of an alkene.

The electrophile $H^+$ from the acid attacks the double bond of 1-methylcyclohexene. According to Markovnikov's rule, protonation occurs at the less substituted carbon (C2) to form the more stable tertiary carbocation at the C1 position (1-methylcyclohexyl cation).

A water molecule acts as a nucleophile and attacks the tertiary carbocation, forming an oxonium ion intermediate.

Deprotonation of the oxonium ion yields the final product, 1-methylcyclohexanol.

The structure of 1-methylcyclohexanol matches the second option.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product obtained when ketone reacts with $\text{NH}_2$-$\text{NH}_2$.
questions.solution:
Ketones react with hydrazine ($H_2N-NH_2$) to form hydrazones.

The reaction proceeds via nucleophilic addition of hydrazine to the carbonyl group, followed by the elimination of a water molecule.

$R_2C=O + H_2N-NH_2 \rightarrow R_2C=N-NH_2 + H_2O$

The resulting product, $R_2C=N-NH_2$, is known as a hydrazone.

Answer: Hydrazone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the reagent used in the transformation of Ketone into semicarbazone.
questions.solution:
The transformation of a ketone into a semicarbazone involves the reaction of the ketone with semicarbazide.

The chemical formula of semicarbazide is $\text{NH}_2-\text{NH}-\text{CONH}_2$.

The reaction proceeds via nucleophilic addition followed by the elimination of a water molecule, resulting in the formation of a semicarbazone ($ \gt \text{C}=\text{N}-\text{NH}-\text{CONH}_2$).

Other reagents given:
$\text{NH}_2-\text{OH}$ (hydroxylamine) forms an oxime.
$\text{NH}_2-\text{NH}_2$ (hydrazine) forms a hydrazone.
$\text{NH}_2-\text{NH}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$ (phenylhydrazine) forms a phenylhydrazone.

Answer: $\text{NH}_2-\text{NH}-\text{CONH}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following reagents is used to prepare alkyl isocyanides from RX?
questions.solution:
Alkyl halides react with alcoholic silver cyanide ($\text{AgCN}$) to form alkyl isocyanides as the major product.

$\text{AgCN}$ is predominantly covalent in nature, so only the nitrogen atom has a lone pair of electrons available for nucleophilic attack. This leads to the formation of an alkyl isocyanide ($\text{RNC}$).

$\text{R-X} + \text{AgCN} \rightarrow \text{R-NC} + \text{AgX}$

In contrast, $\text{KCN}$ gives alkyl cyanides, $\text{KNO}_2$ gives alkyl nitrites, and $\text{AgNO}_2$ gives nitroalkanes.

Answer: AgCN (alco)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions is exhibited only by primary amines?
questions.solution:
Acetylation is given by both primary and secondary amines as they contain replaceable hydrogen atoms on the nitrogen atom.

Alkylation is given by primary, secondary, and tertiary amines to form higher amines and quaternary ammonium salts.

Reaction with nitrous acid is given by primary, secondary, and tertiary amines, though they yield different products (primary amines yield alcohols or diazonium salts, secondary amines yield N-nitrosamines, and tertiary amines yield nitrite salts).

The carbylamine test (isocyanide test) involves heating an amine with chloroform and alcoholic potassium hydroxide. Only primary aliphatic and aromatic amines give this test, producing foul-smelling isocyanides (carbylamines). Secondary and tertiary amines do not respond to this test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reagents is used to convert -CN group to -$\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ group?
questions.solution:
The conversion of a cyano group ($-CN$) to a primary amine group ($-CH_2NH_2$) is a reduction reaction.

Sodium and ethanol ($Na + C_2H_5OH$) act as a reducing agent, providing nascent hydrogen which reduces the nitrile to a primary amine. This reaction is known as the Mendius reduction.

$R-CN + 4[H] \xrightarrow{Na + C_2H_5OH} R-CH_2NH_2$

The other reagents are not reducing agents for this conversion: $CrO_3$ is an oxidizing agent, while $H_3PO_4$ and $Al_2O_3$ are typically used for dehydration.

Answer: $\text{Na} + \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the cation present in chlorophyll in green plants.
questions.solution:
Chlorophyll is a green pigment found in plants, algae, and cyanobacteria, which is essential for photosynthesis.

Structurally, chlorophyll is a coordination complex consisting of a substituted porphyrin ring (specifically a chlorin ring) with a central metal ion.

The central metal ion coordinated in the porphyrin ring of chlorophyll is magnesium, specifically in the $+2$ oxidation state.

Thus, the cation present in chlorophyll is $\text{Mg}^{2+}$.

Answer: $\text{Mg}^{2+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is a globular protein?
questions.solution:
Proteins are classified into fibrous and globular proteins based on their molecular shape.

Fibrous proteins have a fiber-like structure formed by parallel polypeptide chains held together by hydrogen and disulfide bonds. Examples include keratin (found in hair, wool, silk) and myosin (found in muscles).

Globular proteins have a spherical shape formed when the chains of polypeptides coil around. Examples include insulin and albumins.

Thus, insulin is a globular protein.

Answer: Insulin

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which carbon atoms of glucose, numbered from 1 to 6 forms a hemiacetal structure between -CHO and -OH groups.?
questions.solution:
In the open-chain structure of glucose, the aldehyde group (-CHO) is present at C-1.

The cyclic hemiacetal structure is formed by the intramolecular nucleophilic addition of the -OH group at C-5 to the -CHO group at C-1.

This results in the formation of a stable six-membered pyranose ring.

Thus, the -OH group at C-5 is involved in the hemiacetal formation.

Answer: C-5

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the type of hybridization of carbon that is attached to the OH group, in benzylic alcohol?
questions.solution:
The structure of benzylic alcohol is $C_6H_5-CH_2-OH$.

The carbon atom attached to the $-OH$ group is bonded to one carbon atom of the benzene ring, two hydrogen atoms, and one oxygen atom.

Since it forms exactly four sigma bonds and has zero lone pairs, its steric number is $4$.

Therefore, the hybridization of this carbon atom is $sp^3$.

Answer: $sp^3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify a type of order of reaction that its unit of rate constant is mol dm$^{-3}$s$^{-1}$ from the following.
questions.solution:
The general formula for the unit of the rate constant $k$ for an $n$-th order reaction is given by $(\text{concentration})^{1-n} \text{time}^{-1}$.

Using the standard units of concentration as $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ and time as $\text{s}$, the unit of $k$ becomes $(\text{mol dm}^{-3})^{1-n} \text{s}^{-1}$.

The given unit of the rate constant is $\text{mol dm}^{-3}\text{s}^{-1}$.

Comparing the powers of the concentration term, we get:

$1 - n = 1$

$n = 0$

Therefore, the reaction is a zero-order reaction.

Answer: Zero-order reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In first order reaction, 20 % concentration remains after 10 min. What would be the rate constant of reaction if $\log_{10}(5) = 0.6989$?
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction, the rate constant $k$ is given by the formula:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log_{10} \left( \dfrac{[A]_0}{[A]_t} \right)$

Given that $20\%$ concentration remains after $10$ min, we have:

$t = 10$ min

$[A]_t = \dfrac{20}{100} [A]_0 = 0.2 [A]_0$

Substituting these values into the formula:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{10} \log_{10} \left( \dfrac{[A]_0}{0.2 [A]_0} \right)$

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{10} \log_{10}(5)$

Given $\log_{10}(5) = 0.6989$:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{10} \times 0.6989$

$k = 0.2303 \times 0.6989$

$k = 0.1609$ min$^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the reaction, $A + B \rightarrow P$, the rate law is rate $= k[A][B]^2$. The rate of reaction is $0.25 \text{ Ms}^{-1}$ when $[A] = 1$ M, $[B] = 0.2$ M at $25^\circ$C. Calculate the rate constant of the reaction at the same temperature.
questions.solution:
Given rate law is $\text{rate} = k[A][B]^2$.

Substituting the given values:

$0.25 = k(1)(0.2)^2$

$0.25 = k(0.04)$

$k = \dfrac{0.25}{0.04} = 6.25 \text{ M}^{-2}\text{s}^{-1}$

Answer: $6.25 \text{ M}^{-2}\text{s}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the use of antipyretic drugs.
questions.solution:
Antipyretic drugs are chemical substances which are used to lower the body temperature in high fever.

Common examples of antipyretic drugs include paracetamol and aspirin.

Drugs used to kill microorganisms are called antimicrobials or antibiotics.

Drugs used to relieve pain are called analgesics.

Drugs used to prevent pregnancy are called antifertility drugs.

Answer: To reduce fever.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the given ligands, the negative ligand is
questions.solution:
Ammonia ($NH_3$) is a neutral ligand.

Methylamine ($CH_3NH_2$) is a neutral ligand.

Hydrazinium ($NH_2NH_3^+$) is a positive ligand.

Nitrate ($NO_3^-$) is a negative ligand.

Answer: Nitrate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following comparisons is correct for $\Delta_0$ of the following complexes?
I- $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$
II- $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$
III- $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$
IV- $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3+}$
questions.solution:
The crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_0$) depends on several factors, including the oxidation state of the central metal ion and the nature of the ligands.

1. Oxidation state of the metal ion: For the same metal and ligand, $\Delta_0$ increases with an increase in the oxidation state of the central metal ion. This is because a higher charge on the metal ion draws the ligands closer, leading to greater repulsion and a larger splitting of the d-orbitals.
In complex I, Co is in the $+2$ oxidation state: $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$.
In complex II, Co is in the $+3$ oxidation state: $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$.
Therefore, $\Delta_0$ of II $ \gt $ I, which means $\text{I} \lt \text{II}$ is a correct comparison.

2. Nature of the ligand: Strong field ligands cause a larger splitting than weak field ligands. $\text{CN}^-$ is a strong field ligand, whereas $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is a weak field ligand.
Thus, $\Delta_0$ of $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{3+}$ (IV) is significantly greater than that of $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ (II) and $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ (III). The comparison $\text{IV} \lt \text{II}$ is incorrect.

3. The comparison $\text{II} \lt \text{I}$ is incorrect based on the oxidation state rule.

Thus, the most appropriate and direct standard comparison is $\text{I} \lt \text{II}$.

Answer: $\text{I} \lt \text{II}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following elements is doped to a fiber amplifier in an optical fiber communication system?
questions.solution:
In optical fiber communication systems, Erbium (Er) is the most commonly used element for doping fiber amplifiers.

Erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (EDFAs) are widely used because they can amplify light in the $1550$ nm wavelength region, which corresponds to the minimum transmission loss window of silica-based optical fibers.

Answer: Er

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the correct name of law.
"At infinite dilution each ion migrates independent of co-ion and contributes to total molar conductivity of an elctrolyte irrespective of the nature of other ion to which it is associated."
options: Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions
questions.solution: The given statement describes Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions. According to this law, at infinite dilution, when dissociation is complete, each ion makes a definite contribution towards the equivalent or molar conductivity of the electrolyte irrespective of the nature of the other ion with which it is associated.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify from following cell reactions that is spontaneous under standard state of conditions.
questions.solution:
For a cell reaction to be spontaneous under standard conditions, the standard cell potential $E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}}$ must be positive.

$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = E^{\circ}_{\text{cathode}} - E^{\circ}_{\text{anode}}$

Evaluating the given options:

For $\text{Ca(s)} + \text{Cd}^{2+}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{Ca}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + \text{Cd(s)}$:
Cathode (reduction): $\text{Cd}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Cd}$
Anode (oxidation): $\text{Ca} \rightarrow \text{Ca}^{2+}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = -0.403 - (-2.866) = +2.463 \text{ V}$ (Spontaneous)

For $2\text{Br}^-\text{(s)} + \text{Sn}^{2+}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{Br}_2\text{(l)} + \text{Sn(s)}$:
Cathode: $\text{Sn}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Sn}$
Anode: $2\text{Br}^- \rightarrow \text{Br}_2$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = -0.136 - 1.08 = -1.216 \text{ V}$ (Non-spontaneous)

For $2\text{Ag(s)} + \text{Ni}^{2+}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow 2\text{Ag}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{Ni(s)}$:
Cathode: $\text{Ni}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Ni}$
Anode: $\text{Ag} \rightarrow \text{Ag}^+$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = -0.257 - 0.799 = -1.056 \text{ V}$ (Non-spontaneous)

For $2\text{Au(s)} + \text{Zn}^{2+}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow 2\text{Au}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{Zn(s)}$:
Cathode: $\text{Zn}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Zn}$
Anode: $\text{Au} \rightarrow \text{Au}^+$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{cell}} = -0.763 - 1.68 = -2.443 \text{ V}$ (Non-spontaneous)

The only reaction with a positive standard cell potential is the first one.

Answer: $\text{Ca(s)} + \text{Cd}^{2+}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{Ca}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + \text{Cd(s)}$, $[E^0_{\text{Ca}} = -2.866$ V & $E^0_{\text{Cd}} = -0.403$ V$]$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Calculate the molar conductivity of 0.2 M KCl solution at 298 K ($k = 0.0248 \ \Omega^{-1}$cm$^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
Given concentration $C = 0.2$ M and conductivity $k = 0.0248 \ \Omega^{-1}$ cm$^{-1}$.

The formula for molar conductivity is $\Lambda_m = \dfrac{k \times 1000}{C}$.

Substituting the given values:

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{0.0248 \times 1000}{0.2}$

$\Lambda_m = \dfrac{24.8}{0.2} = 124 \ \Omega^{-1}$ cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$.

Answer: $124 \ \Omega^{-1}$ cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The cyclic $\pi$-molecular orbital formed by overlap of p-orbitals must contain,
questions.solution:
According to H\u00fcckel's rule, a cyclic, planar, and completely conjugated system is highly stable and aromatic if it contains $(4n + 2)\pi$-electrons, where $n$ is an integer ($0, 1, 2, \dots$).

These $\pi$-electrons reside in the cyclic $\pi$-molecular orbital formed by the continuous lateral overlap of unhybridized p-orbitals of the atoms in the ring.

Thus, the cyclic $\pi$-molecular orbital must contain $(4n + 2)$ p electrons for the system to exhibit aromatic stability.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are TRUE?
(I) Inductive effect operates through the sigma bond
(II) Resonance effect operates through the pi bond
(III) Inductive effects operate through the pi bond
(IV) Resonance effect operates through the sigma bond
questions.solution:
Inductive effect involves the displacement of $\sigma$-electrons along a saturated carbon chain. Thus, it operates through $\sigma$-bonds.

Resonance effect involves the delocalization of $\pi$-electrons or lone pairs of electrons. Thus, it operates through $\pi$-bonds.

Therefore, statements (I) and (II) are true.

Answer: (I) and (II)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the false statement regarding chirality from the following.
options: $SN^1$ reaction yields 1:1 mixture of both enantiomers
A recemic mixture shows zero dipole rotation
Enantiomers are superimposable mirror images of each other
The product obtained by $SN^2$ reaction of haloalkane having chirality at the reactive site shows inversion of configuration
questions.solution:
Enantiomers are defined as stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other. Therefore, the statement that enantiomers are superimposable mirror images is false.

In an $S_N1$ reaction, the formation of a planar carbocation intermediate allows the nucleophile to attack from either face with equal probability, generally yielding a 1:1 mixture of enantiomers (a racemic mixture).

A racemic mixture contains equal amounts of dextrorotatory and levorotatory enantiomers, resulting in zero net optical rotation.

In an $S_N2$ reaction at a chiral center, the nucleophile attacks from the side opposite to the leaving group, leading to a complete inversion of configuration.

Answer: Enantiomers are superimposable mirror images of each other

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is obtained when Bromoethane is reacted with silver acetate?
questions.solution:
The reaction between bromoethane and silver acetate is a nucleophilic substitution reaction.

The acetate ion ($CH_3COO^-$) acts as a nucleophile and attacks the electrophilic carbon of bromoethane ($CH_3CH_2Br$), displacing the bromide ion.

The chemical equation for the reaction is:
$CH_3CH_2Br + CH_3COOAg \rightarrow CH_3COOCH_2CH_3 + AgBr \downarrow$

The product formed is $CH_3COOCH_2CH_3$, which is ethyl acetate.

Answer: ethyl acetate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the reagent used in Etard reaction
questions.solution:
The Etard reaction involves the oxidation of a methyl group attached to an aromatic ring (such as toluene) to an aldehyde group (such as benzaldehyde).

The reagent used for this specific transformation is chromyl chloride ($CrO_2Cl_2$) in a non-polar solvent like $CS_2$ or $CCl_4$, followed by hydrolysis.

The reaction proceeds via the formation of a brown chromium complex, which upon decomposition with water yields the corresponding aldehyde.

Answer: Chromyl chloride

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following sentences is true for a basic solution?
options: In basic solution, the excess of $\text{OH}^-$ ions are present.
In the basic solution, there is excess of $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ ions.
The pOH of a basic solution can be calculated by pOH = $-\log[\text{H}^+]$
questions.solution:
In a neutral solution, $[\text{H}_3\text{O}^+] = [\text{OH}^-]$.

In an acidic solution, $[\text{H}_3\text{O}^+] \gt [\text{OH}^-]$, meaning there is an excess of $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ ions.

In a basic solution, $[\text{OH}^-] \gt [\text{H}_3\text{O}^+]$, meaning there is an excess of $\text{OH}^-$ ions.

The pOH of any solution is defined as $\text{pOH} = -\log[\text{OH}^-]$.

Thus, the only true statement is that in a basic solution, an excess of $\text{OH}^-$ ions are present.

Answer: In basic solution, the excess of $\text{OH}^-$ ions are present.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the relationship between the degree of dissociation of a weak base and its concentration?
options: The degree of dissociation of a weak base is directly proportional to square root of its concentration.
The degree of dissociation of a weak base is inversely proportional to square root of its concentration.
The degree of dissociation of a weak base doesn't depend on concentration.
The degree of dissociation of a weak base is directly proportional to its concentration
questions.solution:
For a weak base $BOH$, the dissociation reaction is $BOH \rightleftharpoons B^+ + OH^-$.

Let the initial concentration be $C$ and the degree of dissociation be $\alpha$.

At equilibrium, the concentrations are $[BOH] = C(1-\alpha)$, $[B^+] = C\alpha$, and $[OH^-] = C\alpha$.

The base dissociation constant $K_b$ is given by $K_b = \dfrac{[B^+][OH^-]}{[BOH]} = \dfrac{C\alpha \cdot C\alpha}{C(1-\alpha)} = \dfrac{C\alpha^2}{1-\alpha}$.

For a weak base, $\alpha$ is very small compared to $1$, so $1-\alpha \approx 1$.

Thus, $K_b \approx C\alpha^2 \Rightarrow \alpha = \sqrt{\dfrac{K_b}{C}}$.

Therefore, the degree of dissociation of a weak base is inversely proportional to the square root of its concentration.

Answer: The degree of dissociation of a weak base is inversely proportional to square root of its concentration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A weak monobasic acid is 0.04 % dissociated in 0.25 M solution. What is pH of the solution?
questions.solution:
Given concentration of the weak monobasic acid, $C = 0.25$ M.

Degree of dissociation, $\alpha = 0.04\% = \dfrac{0.04}{100} = 4 \times 10^{-4}$.

For a weak monobasic acid, the hydrogen ion concentration is given by:

$[H^+] = C\alpha$

Substituting the values:

$[H^+] = 0.25 \times 4 \times 10^{-4} = 10^{-4}$ M.

The pH of the solution is:

$pH = -\log[H^+]$

$pH = -\log(10^{-4}) = 4$.

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct decreasing order of oxidizing power of perhalate ions?
questions.solution:
The oxidizing power of perhalate ions depends on their standard reduction potentials. A higher positive standard reduction potential indicates a stronger oxidizing agent.

The standard reduction potentials ($E^{\circ}$) for the reduction of perhalate ions to halate ions in acidic medium are:
$E^{\circ}(\text{BrO}_4^- / \text{BrO}_3^-) = +1.74\text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}(\text{IO}_4^- / \text{IO}_3^-) = +1.65\text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}(\text{ClO}_4^- / \text{ClO}_3^-) = +1.20\text{ V}$

Since the reduction potential is highest for $\text{BrO}_4^-$ and lowest for $\text{ClO}_4^-$, the decreasing order of oxidizing power is $\text{BrO}_4^- \gt \text{IO}_4^- \gt \text{ClO}_4^-$.

The exceptionally high oxidizing power of $\text{BrO}_4^-$ is due to the relative instability of the $+7$ oxidation state of bromine, which arises from the poor shielding of the $3d$ electrons (d-block contraction or middle row anomaly).

Answer: $\text{BrO}_4^- \gt \text{IO}_4^- \gt \text{ClO}_4^-$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the Charring process, concentrated sulfuric acid reacts with sugar to give sugar charcoal. What is the role of conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in this reaction?
questions.solution:
The reaction of concentrated sulfuric acid with sugar (sucrose) is known as the charring process.

$\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4} 12\text{C} + 11\text{H}_2\text{O}$

In this reaction, concentrated sulfuric acid removes water molecules from the sugar molecule, leaving behind a black mass of elemental carbon, which is called sugar charcoal. This demonstrates the strong affinity of concentrated sulfuric acid for water.

Therefore, concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ acts as a strong dehydrating agent.

Answer: A dehydrating agent

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of polymer the natural rubber is?
questions.solution:
Natural rubber is an addition polymer of isoprene (2-methyl-1,3-butadiene). It has weak intermolecular forces of attraction (van der Waals forces) between its polymer chains, which permit the polymer to be stretched. A few cross-links are introduced between the chains, which help the polymer retract to its original position after the force is released. Polymers with such elastic properties are classified as elastomers.

Therefore, natural rubber is an elastomer.

Answer: Elastomer

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the monomer used to prepare orlon.
questions.solution:
Orlon is the trade name for polyacrylonitrile (PAN).

It is an addition polymer formed by the polymerisation of acrylonitrile.

The chemical reaction is:

$n CH_2=CH-CN \xrightarrow{\text{Polymerisation}} [-CH_2-CH(CN)-]_n$

Thus, the monomer used to prepare orlon is acrylonitrile.

Answer: acrylonitrile

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a redox reaction?
questions.solution:
In the reaction $\text{Zn} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{ZnSO}_4 + \text{H}_2$, the oxidation state of Zn changes from $0$ to $+2$ and H changes from $+1$ to $0$. It is a redox reaction.

In the reaction $\text{Al(OH)}_3 + 3\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{AlCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$, the oxidation states of all elements remain the same (Al is $+3$, O is $-2$, H is $+1$, Cl is $-1$). It is an acid-base neutralization reaction, not a redox reaction.

In the reaction $\text{Mg} + 1/2 \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{Mg}^{2+} + \text{O}^{2-}$, the oxidation state of Mg changes from $0$ to $+2$ and O changes from $0$ to $-2$. It is a redox reaction.

In the reaction $\text{Fe}_{(s)} + \text{Cu}^{2+}_{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{2+}_{(aq)} + \text{Cu}_{(s)}$, the oxidation state of Fe changes from $0$ to $+2$ and Cu changes from $+2$ to $0$. It is a redox reaction.

Answer: $\text{Al(OH)}_3 + 3\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{AlCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following dopant is NOT used in Ge to obtain n-type semiconductor?
questions.solution:
Ge is a Group 14 element.

To obtain an n-type semiconductor, Ge must be doped with a pentavalent impurity (Group 15 element) such as P, As, or Sb.

Boron (B) is a trivalent impurity (Group 13 element). Doping Ge with B results in a p-type semiconductor.

Therefore, B is not used to obtain an n-type semiconductor.

Answer: B

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A compound formed by elements A and B crystallizes in a cubic structure where A atoms are at the corner of the cube and B atoms are at the center of the cube. What is the formula of the compound?
questions.solution:
Number of A atoms per unit cell = $8 \times \dfrac{1}{8} = 1$

Number of B atoms per unit cell = $1 \times 1 = 1$

Ratio of A to B is $1:1$.

The formula of the compound is $\text{AB}$.

Answer: $\text{AB}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An element with a molar mass 27g mol$^{-1}$ forms a cubic unit cell. Calculate the number of atoms present in a unit cell if the density of metal is 2.7g cm$^{-3}$.
$[a^3 \times N_A = 40$ cm$^3$ mol$^{-1}]$
questions.solution:
The density of a cubic unit cell is given by the formula:

$d = \dfrac{Z \times M}{a^3 \times N_A}$

where $Z$ is the number of atoms per unit cell, $M$ is the molar mass, $a$ is the edge length, and $N_A$ is Avogadro's number.

Rearranging the formula to solve for $Z$:

$Z = \dfrac{d \times (a^3 \times N_A)}{M}$

Substituting the given values $d = 2.7$ g cm$^{-3}$, $M = 27$ g mol$^{-1}$, and $a^3 \times N_A = 40$ cm$^3$ mol$^{-1}$:

$Z = \dfrac{2.7 \times 40}{27}$

$Z = \dfrac{108}{27} = 4$

The number of atoms present in the unit cell is $4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify a pair of gases from following that does not obey Henry's law.
questions.solution:
Henry's law is applicable only to those gases which do not react chemically with the solvent and do not undergo dissociation or association in the solution.

Gases like $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{CO}_2$ react with water to form $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ and $\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$ respectively.

$\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^-$

$\text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{HCO}_3^-$

Due to their chemical reaction with the solvent, their solubility is exceptionally high and they do not obey Henry's law.

Gases like $\text{O}_2$, $\text{N}_2$, and $\text{CH}_4$ do not react with water and thus obey Henry's law.

Answer: $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{CO}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following aqueous solutions will show maximum vapour pressure at 300K?
questions.solution:
Relative lowering of vapour pressure is a colligative property, which depends on the number of solute particles in the solution.

$\Delta P \propto i \times C$

For maximum vapour pressure, the lowering of vapour pressure ($\Delta P$) must be minimum, which means the van't Hoff factor ($i$) should be minimum (since concentration $C$ is $1$ M for all options).

For NaCl, $i = 2$
For $\text{CaCl}_2$, $i = 3$
For $\text{AlCl}_3$, $i = 4$
For $\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}$ (sucrose), $i = 1$

Since sucrose has the minimum value of $i$, its solution will have the minimum lowering of vapour pressure and hence the maximum vapour pressure.

Answer: $1$ M $\text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{22}\text{O}_{11}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
2 g nonelectrolyte solute when dissolved in 50 g water increases its boiling point by 0.13 K.
Calculate the molar mass of solute if molal elevation constant of water is 0.52 K kg mol$^{-1}$
questions.solution:
The elevation in boiling point is given by the formula:

$\Delta T_b = K_b \times m$

where $m$ is the molality of the solution, which can be expressed as:

$m = \dfrac{w_2 \times 1000}{M_2 \times w_1}$

Substituting the expression for molality into the boiling point elevation formula gives:

$\Delta T_b = \dfrac{K_b \times w_2 \times 1000}{M_2 \times w_1}$

Rearranging to solve for the molar mass of the solute, $M_2$:

$M_2 = \dfrac{K_b \times w_2 \times 1000}{\Delta T_b \times w_1}$

Substituting the given values ($K_b = 0.52$ K kg mol$^{-1}$, $w_2 = 2$ g, $\Delta T_b = 0.13$ K, $w_1 = 50$ g):

$M_2 = \dfrac{0.52 \times 2 \times 1000}{0.13 \times 50}$

$M_2 = 4 \times 40 = 160$ g/mol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following contains maximum number of molecules?
questions.solution:
The number of molecules is directly proportional to the number of moles.

Number of moles of $\text{H}_2$ in $0.4$ g = $\dfrac{0.4}{2} = 0.2$ mol

Number of moles of $\text{O}_2$ in $3.2$ g = $\dfrac{3.2}{32} = 0.1$ mol

Number of moles of $\text{H}_2$ in $16.8 \text{ dm}^3$ at STP = $\dfrac{16.8}{22.4} = 0.75$ mol

Number of moles of $\text{O}_2$ in $11.2 \text{ dm}^3$ at STP = $\dfrac{11.2}{22.4} = 0.5$ mol

Since $0.75$ mol is the maximum among the given options, $16.8 \text{ dm}^3$ of $\text{H}_2$ gas at STP contains the maximum number of molecules.

Answer: $16.8 \text{ dm}^3$ of $\text{H}_2$ gas at STP

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the temperature of 2 moles of gas occupying a volume of 5.0 liters at 24.6 atmospheres?
($R = 0.0821$ L atm K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
Using the ideal gas equation $PV = nRT$

Substituting the given values:

$24.6 \times 5.0 = 2 \times 0.0821 \times T$

$123 = 0.1642 \times T$

$T = \dfrac{123}{0.1642} = 749.08$ K

Converting to Celsius:

$T = 749.08 - 273.15 = 475.93^{\circ}\text{C} \approx 476^{\circ}\text{C}$

Answer: $476^\circ$C

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following pairs represents isobars?
questions.solution:
Isobars are atoms of different elements having the same mass number but different atomic numbers.

In the pair ${}^{40}\text{K}_{19}$ and ${}^{40}\text{Ca}_{20}$, both have the same mass number $40$ but different atomic numbers $19$ and $20$ respectively.

Thus, they represent a pair of isobars.

Answer: ${}^{40}\text{K}_{19}$ and ${}^{40}\text{Ca}_{20}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The electronic configurations of elements are as-
$A = 1s^2 \ 2s^2 \ 2p^6 \ 3s^2 \ 3p^6 \ 4s^2$
$B = 1s^2 \ 2s^2 \ 2p^6 \ 3s^2 \ 3p^5$
Which of the following is formula of ionic compound that could be formed between these two elements A and B?
questions.solution:
Element A has the electronic configuration $1s^2 \ 2s^2 \ 2p^6 \ 3s^2 \ 3p^6 \ 4s^2$. It has $2$ valence electrons in its outermost shell, so it loses $2$ electrons to achieve a stable noble gas configuration, forming the $\text{A}^{2+}$ ion.

Element B has the electronic configuration $1s^2 \ 2s^2 \ 2p^6 \ 3s^2 \ 3p^5$. It has $7$ valence electrons in its outermost shell, so it gains $1$ electron to achieve a stable noble gas configuration, forming the $\text{B}^{-}$ ion.

To form a neutral ionic compound, one $\text{A}^{2+}$ ion combines with two $\text{B}^{-}$ ions.

The formula of the compound is $\text{AB}_2$.

Answer: $\text{AB}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the atomic number of an element having $ns^1$ electronic configuration and belonging to 3d transition series?
questions.solution:
The 3d transition series belongs to the 4th period, so $n=4$.

The general electronic configuration of the 3d transition series is $[Ar] 3d^{1-10} 4s^{1-2}$.

Elements with an $ns^1$ (i.e., $4s^1$) configuration in this series are Chromium (Cr) and Copper (Cu) due to the extra stability of half-filled and fully-filled d-subshells.

The electronic configuration of Cr ($Z=24$) is $[Ar] 3d^5 4s^1$.

The electronic configuration of Cu ($Z=29$) is $[Ar] 3d^{10} 4s^1$.

Thus, the atomic numbers are 24 and 29.

Answer: 24 and 29

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct statement regarding lyophilic colloid from the following.
options: It is formed only by special methods.
questions.solution:
The word lyophilic means liquid-loving or solvent-loving. Therefore, lyophilic colloids are solvent-loving colloids.

They are reversible in nature because if the dispersion medium is separated from the dispersed phase, the sol can be reconstituted by simply remixing with the dispersion medium.

They can be prepared easily by directly mixing the dispersed phase with the dispersion medium, without requiring any special methods.

Answer: It is solvent loving colloid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct for the spontaneous adsorption of a gas?
options: $\Delta S$ is negative and, therefore $\Delta H$ should be highly positive
$\Delta S$ is negative and therefore, $\Delta H$ should be highly negative.
$\Delta S$ is positive and therefore, $\Delta H$ should be negative.
$\Delta S$ is positive and therefore, $\Delta H$ should also be highly positive.
questions.solution:
During the adsorption of a gas, the gas molecules are restricted to the surface of the solid, which decreases their randomness or entropy. Thus, the change in entropy, $\Delta S$, is negative.

For a process to be spontaneous, the change in Gibbs free energy, $\Delta G$, must be negative.

According to the Gibbs-Helmholtz equation:
$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$

Since $\Delta S$ is negative, the term $-T\Delta S$ becomes positive. For $\Delta G$ to be negative, the enthalpy change, $\Delta H$, must be negative and its magnitude must be large enough to overcome the positive $-T\Delta S$ term.

Therefore, $\Delta S$ is negative and $\Delta H$ should be highly negative.

Answer: $\Delta S$ is negative and therefore, $\Delta H$ should be highly negative.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the dimensional nature of nanoparticles by the following.
questions.solution:
Nanomaterials are classified based on the number of dimensions that are not confined to the nanoscale range ($1-100$ nm).

Zero-dimensional ($0$D) nanomaterials have all three dimensions in the nanoscale. Examples include nanoparticles, quantum dots, and fullerenes.

One-dimensional ($1$D) nanomaterials have two dimensions in the nanoscale. Examples include nanotubes and nanowires.

Two-dimensional ($2$D) nanomaterials have one dimension in the nanoscale. Examples include graphene and nanofilms.

Since nanoparticles have all three dimensions in the nanoscale, they are classified as zero-dimensional.

Answer: zero dimensional

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the enthalpy change of the reaction,
$\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{HCl(g)}$
if bond energies (kJ mol$^{-1}$):
H–H = 436, Cl–Cl = 242, H–Cl = 431
questions.solution:
The enthalpy change of the reaction is given by the difference between the sum of bond energies of reactants and the sum of bond energies of products.

$\Delta H = \sum \text{BE(Reactants)} - \sum \text{BE(Products)}$

For the given reaction:
$\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{HCl(g)}$

$\Delta H = [\text{BE(H-H)} + \text{BE(Cl-Cl)}] - [2 \times \text{BE(H-Cl)}]$

Substituting the given values:
$\Delta H = (436 + 242) - (2 \times 431)$

$\Delta H = 678 - 862$

$\Delta H = -184 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $-184$ kJ/mol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For a certain reaction $\Delta H = -50$ kJ and $\Delta S = -100$ J/K find the temperature so that the reaction is spontaneous.
questions.solution:
For a reaction to be spontaneous, the change in Gibbs free energy must be negative, i.e., $\Delta G \lt 0$.

Using the Gibbs free energy equation:

$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$

Substituting the given values ($\Delta H = -50000$ J and $\Delta S = -100$ J/K):

$-50000 - T(-100) \lt 0$

$-50000 + 100T \lt 0$

$100T \lt 50000$

$T \lt 500$ K

The reaction is spontaneous at temperatures below $500$ K. Among the given options, only $450$ K satisfies this condition.

Answer: $450$ K

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If a spherical balloon has a variable diameter $3x + \dfrac{9}{2}$ units, then the rate of change of its volume with respect to $x$ is
questions.solution:
Given the diameter of the spherical balloon is $D = 3x + \dfrac{9}{2} = \dfrac{3(2x + 3)}{2}$

The radius of the balloon is $r = \dfrac{D}{2} = \dfrac{3(2x + 3)}{4}$

The volume of the spherical balloon is $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$

Substituting the value of $r$:

$V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi \left( \dfrac{3(2x + 3)}{4} \right)^3$

$V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi \left( \dfrac{27(2x + 3)^3}{64} \right)$

$V = \dfrac{9\pi}{16}(2x + 3)^3$

Differentiating the volume with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dV}{dx} = \dfrac{9\pi}{16} \cdot 3(2x + 3)^2 \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}(2x + 3)$

$\dfrac{dV}{dx} = \dfrac{27\pi}{16}(2x + 3)^2 \cdot 2$

$\dfrac{dV}{dx} = \dfrac{27\pi}{8}(2x + 3)^2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A wire 40 metre in length is to be cut into two pieces. One piece is formed into a square and the other piece into a circle. The lengths of the two pieces so that the combined area of the square and the circle is minimum, are respectively
questions.solution:
Let the length of the piece for the square be $x$ and for the circle be $40 - x$.

Perimeter of the square $= x \Rightarrow$ side $= \dfrac{x}{4}$

Area of the square, $A_1 = \dfrac{x^2}{16}$

Circumference of the circle $= 40 - x \Rightarrow$ radius $r = \dfrac{40 - x}{2\pi}$

Area of the circle, $A_2 = \pi r^2 = \dfrac{(40 - x)^2}{4\pi}$

Total area, $A = \dfrac{x^2}{16} + \dfrac{(40 - x)^2}{4\pi}$

For minimum area, $\dfrac{dA}{dx} = 0$

$\dfrac{2x}{16} - \dfrac{2(40 - x)}{4\pi} = 0$

$\dfrac{x}{8} = \dfrac{40 - x}{2\pi}$

$\pi x = 160 - 4x$

$x(\pi + 4) = 160 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{160}{\pi + 4}$

Length of the other piece $= 40 - x = 40 - \dfrac{160}{\pi + 4} = \dfrac{40\pi}{\pi + 4}$

Since $\dfrac{d^2A}{dx^2} = \dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \gt 0$, the area is minimum for these lengths.

Answer: $\dfrac{160}{\pi + 4}, \dfrac{40\pi}{\pi + 4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the normal to the curve $xy + 7 = 0$ is $Ax + By + C = 0$, then
questions.solution:
The given equation of the curve is $xy + 7 = 0$.

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$x \dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{y}{x}$

Substituting $y = -\dfrac{7}{x}$, we get:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{7}{x^2}$

Since $x^2 \gt 0$ for all $x \neq 0$, the slope of the tangent $\dfrac{dy}{dx} \gt 0$.

The slope of the normal is given by $-\dfrac{dx}{dy} = -\dfrac{x^2}{7} \lt 0$.

The given equation of the normal is $Ax + By + C = 0$, which has a slope of $-\dfrac{A}{B}$.

Equating the slopes, we have:

$-\dfrac{A}{B} \lt 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{A}{B} \gt 0$

This implies that $A$ and $B$ must have the same sign. Therefore, either $A \gt 0, B \gt 0$ or $A \lt 0, B \lt 0$.

Answer: $A \gt 0, B \gt 0$ or $A \lt 0, B \lt 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region (in sq.units) bounded by the curve $y = 2\sqrt{1 - x^2}$ and the X-axis is _____
questions.solution:
The given curve is $y = 2\sqrt{1 - x^2}$.

Squaring both sides, we get $y^2 = 4(1 - x^2) \Rightarrow x^2 + \dfrac{y^2}{4} = 1$.

This represents an ellipse with semi-minor axis $a = 1$ and semi-major axis $b = 2$.

Since $y \ge 0$, the given curve represents the upper half of the ellipse.

The area of the complete ellipse is $\pi a b = \pi(1)(2) = 2\pi$.

Therefore, the area of the upper half of the ellipse is $\dfrac{1}{2}(2\pi) = \pi$.

Alternatively, the area can be found by integration:

Area $= \int_{-1}^{1} 2\sqrt{1 - x^2} dx$

Area $= 2 \left[ \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{1 - x^2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{-1}x \right]_{-1}^{1}$

Area $= 2 \left[ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \right] = \pi$ sq. units.

Answer: $\pi$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If a circle with center $(-1, 1)$ touches the line $x + 2y + 4 = 0$, then the co-ordinates of the point of contact are
questions.solution:
The point of contact is the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the center of the circle to the tangent line.

The coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular $(h, k)$ from a point $(x_1, y_1)$ to the line $ax + by + c = 0$ are given by:

$\dfrac{h - x_1}{a} = \dfrac{k - y_1}{b} = -\dfrac{ax_1 + by_1 + c}{a^2 + b^2}$

Substituting $(x_1, y_1) = (-1, 1)$ and the line equation $x + 2y + 4 = 0$:

$\dfrac{h - (-1)}{1} = \dfrac{k - 1}{2} = -\dfrac{1(-1) + 2(1) + 4}{1^2 + 2^2}$

$\dfrac{h + 1}{1} = \dfrac{k - 1}{2} = -\dfrac{5}{5} = -1$

$h + 1 = -1 \Rightarrow h = -2$

$\dfrac{k - 1}{2} = -1 \Rightarrow k - 1 = -2 \Rightarrow k = -1$

The coordinates of the point of contact are $(-2, -1)$.

Answer: $(-2, -1)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The polar form of the complex number $z = \dfrac{1}{1 + i}$, (where $i = \sqrt{-1}$) is
questions.solution:
$z = \dfrac{1}{1 + i}$

Multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator:

$z = \dfrac{1(1 - i)}{(1 + i)(1 - i)} = \dfrac{1 - i}{1^2 - i^2} = \dfrac{1 - i}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}i$

The modulus of $z$ is:

$r = |z| = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{4}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

The argument of $z$ is:

$\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{-1/2}{1/2}\right) = \tan^{-1}(-1)$

Since $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant, $\theta = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{7\pi}{4}$.

Thus, the polar form of $z$ is:

$z = r(\cos \theta + i \sin \theta) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\cos \dfrac{7\pi}{4} + i \sin \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\right)$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\cos \dfrac{7\pi}{4} + i \sin \dfrac{7\pi}{4}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{(8 - 2x)^{\frac{1}{3}} - 2}{3 - (243 + 5x)^{\frac{1}{5}}}, & \text{if } x \neq 0 \\ k, & \text{if } x = 0 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 0$, then $k =$
questions.solution:
Since the function $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = 0$, we have $k = \lim_{x \to 0} f(x)$.

$k = \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{(8 - 2x)^{1/3} - 2}{3 - (243 + 5x)^{1/5}}$

This is a $\dfrac{0}{0}$ form. Applying L'Hospital's Rule, we differentiate the numerator and the denominator with respect to $x$:

$k = \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{3}(8 - 2x)^{-2/3}(-2)}{-\dfrac{1}{5}(243 + 5x)^{-4/5}(5)}$

Substituting $x = 0$ into the expression:

$k = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{3}(8)^{-2/3}(-2)}{-(243)^{-4/5}}$

$k = \dfrac{-\dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{4}}{-\dfrac{1}{81}}$

$k = \dfrac{-\dfrac{1}{6}}{-\dfrac{1}{81}}$

$k = \dfrac{81}{6} = \dfrac{27}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of the integral $\displaystyle\int_{-\sqrt{3}}^{\sqrt{3}} \dfrac{(2x^9 + 3x^8 - 5x^7 + 9x^6 + 4x^3 - x + 3)}{x^2 + 3} \, dx$ is
questions.solution:
Let the given integral be $I$. We can split the integrand into odd and even functions:

$I = \displaystyle\int_{-\sqrt{3}}^{\sqrt{3}} \dfrac{2x^9 - 5x^7 + 4x^3 - x}{x^2 + 3} \, dx + \displaystyle\int_{-\sqrt{3}}^{\sqrt{3}} \dfrac{3x^8 + 9x^6 + 3}{x^2 + 3} \, dx$

The first integral is $0$ because the integrand is an odd function and the limits are symmetric about the origin.

For the second integral, simplifying the integrand gives:

$I = \displaystyle\int_{-\sqrt{3}}^{\sqrt{3}} \dfrac{3x^6(x^2 + 3) + 3}{x^2 + 3} \, dx = \displaystyle\int_{-\sqrt{3}}^{\sqrt{3}} \left( 3x^6 + \dfrac{3}{x^2 + 3} \right) \, dx$

Since the integrand is an even function, we can write:

$I = 2 \displaystyle\int_{0}^{\sqrt{3}} \left( 3x^6 + \dfrac{3}{x^2 + 3} \right) \, dx$

Integrating with respect to $x$:

$I = 2 \left[ \dfrac{3x^7}{7} + \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{3}} \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3}}\right) \right]_0^{\sqrt{3}}$

Substituting the limits:

$I = 2 \left( \dfrac{3(\sqrt{3})^7}{7} + \sqrt{3} \tan^{-1}(1) - 0 \right)$

Using $(\sqrt{3})^7 = 27\sqrt{3}$ and $\tan^{-1}(1) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$:

$I = 2 \left( \dfrac{3 \times 27\sqrt{3}}{7} + \sqrt{3} \dfrac{\pi}{4} \right)$

$I = \dfrac{162\sqrt{3}}{7} + \sqrt{3} \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{162\sqrt{3}}{7} + \sqrt{3} \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\displaystyle\int_0^a \dfrac{dx}{1 + 4x^2} = \dfrac{\pi}{8}$, then $a =$
questions.solution:
Given $\displaystyle\int_0^a \dfrac{dx}{1 + 4x^2} = \dfrac{\pi}{8}$

Let $2x = t \Rightarrow 2dx = dt$

When $x = 0$, $t = 0$ and when $x = a$, $t = 2a$

The integral becomes $\dfrac{1}{2} \displaystyle\int_0^{2a} \dfrac{dt}{1 + t^2} = \dfrac{\pi}{8}$

$\dfrac{1}{2} [\tan^{-1} t]_0^{2a} = \dfrac{\pi}{8}$

$\dfrac{1}{2} \tan^{-1}(2a) = \dfrac{\pi}{8}$

$\tan^{-1}(2a) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$2a = \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 1$

$a = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A spherical balloon expands at a rate proportional to its surface area. Initially its radius is 2 cm and 5 minutes later it increases upto 7 cm, then surface area of spherical balloon after 12 minutes will be
questions.solution:
Let $V$ be the volume and $S$ be the surface area of the spherical balloon.

Given that the balloon expands at a rate proportional to its surface area:

$\dfrac{dV}{dt} \propto S$

$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = kS$

Using $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ and $S = 4\pi r^2$, differentiating $V$ with respect to $t$ gives:

$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi r^2 \dfrac{dr}{dt} = S \dfrac{dr}{dt}$

Equating the two expressions for $\dfrac{dV}{dt}$:

$S \dfrac{dr}{dt} = kS \Rightarrow \dfrac{dr}{dt} = k$

Integrating both sides with respect to $t$:

$r = kt + C$

Initially, at $t = 0$, $r = 2$ cm:

$2 = k(0) + C \Rightarrow C = 2$

At $t = 5$ minutes, $r = 7$ cm:

$7 = 5k + 2 \Rightarrow 5k = 5 \Rightarrow k = 1$

Thus, the radius at any time $t$ is given by:

$r = t + 2$

After $12$ minutes ($t = 12$):

$r = 12 + 2 = 14$ cm

The surface area of the balloon at $t = 12$ minutes is:

$S = 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times (14)^2$

$S = 4 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 196 = 4 \times 22 \times 28 = 2464$ sq.cm.

Answer: $2464$ sq.cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x+y}{x-y}$ is
options: $c(x^2 + y^2)^{\frac{1}{2}} + e^{\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{y^2}{x}\right)} = 0$, where c is an arbitrary constant
$c(x^2 + y^2)^{\frac{1}{2}} = e^{\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)}$, where c is an arbitrary constant
$c(x^2 - y^2) = e^{\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)}$, where c is an arbitrary constant
$c(x^2 + y^2) = e^{\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)}$, where c is an arbitrary constant
questions.solution:
The given differential equation is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x+y}{x-y}$.

Substituting $y = vx$, we get $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$.

$v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{x+vx}{x-vx} = \dfrac{1+v}{1-v}$

$x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{1+v}{1-v} - v = \dfrac{1+v-v+v^2}{1-v} = \dfrac{1+v^2}{1-v}$

Separating the variables, we get:

$\dfrac{1-v}{1+v^2} dv = \dfrac{dx}{x}$

Integrating both sides:

$\int \dfrac{1}{1+v^2} dv - \int \dfrac{v}{1+v^2} dv = \int \dfrac{dx}{x}$

$\tan^{-1}v - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(1+v^2) = \ln|x| + C$

Substituting $v = \dfrac{y}{x}$:

$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(1+\dfrac{y^2}{x^2}\right) = \ln|x| + C$

$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(\dfrac{x^2+y^2}{x^2}\right) = \ln|x| + C$

$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(x^2+y^2) + \ln|x| = \ln|x| + C$

$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(x^2+y^2) = C$

$\ln(x^2+y^2)^{\dfrac{1}{2}} = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) - C$

$(x^2+y^2)^{\dfrac{1}{2}} = e^{\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) - C}$

$e^C (x^2+y^2)^{\dfrac{1}{2}} = e^{\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)}$

Letting $c = e^C$, we obtain:

Answer: $c(x^2 + y^2)^{\frac{1}{2}} = e^{\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)}$, where c is an arbitrary constant

questions.q: If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y + 5$ and $y(0) = 4$ then $y(\log 2)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y + 5$

Separating the variables gives

$\dfrac{dy}{y + 5} = dx$

Integrating both sides gives

$\int \dfrac{dy}{y + 5} = \int dx$

$\log|y + 5| = x + C$

Using the initial condition $y(0) = 4$ gives

$\log(4 + 5) = 0 + C \Rightarrow C = \log 9$

Substituting $C$ back into the equation gives

$\log(y + 5) = x + \log 9$

$y + 5 = e^{x + \log 9} = 9e^x$

$y = 9e^x - 5$

Substituting $x = \log 2$ gives

$y(\log 2) = 9e^{\log 2} - 5$

$y(\log 2) = 9(2) - 5 = 13$

Answer: $13$

$g'(x) = 2[4h(x) - 2] \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}[4h(x) - 2]$

Answer: $-224$

questions.q: If $y = x + e^x$, then $\dfrac{d^2 x}{dy^2}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given $y = x + e^x$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + e^x$

Taking the reciprocal:

$\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{1}{1 + e^x}$

Differentiating with respect to $y$:

$\dfrac{d^2 x}{dy^2} = \dfrac{d}{dy} \left( \dfrac{dx}{dy} \right) = \dfrac{d}{dx} \left( \dfrac{dx}{dy} \right) \cdot \dfrac{dx}{dy}$

Substituting the values:

$\dfrac{d^2 x}{dy^2} = \dfrac{d}{dx} \left( \dfrac{1}{1 + e^x} \right) \cdot \left( \dfrac{1}{1 + e^x} \right)$

$\dfrac{d^2 x}{dy^2} = \left( \dfrac{-e^x}{(1 + e^x)^2} \right) \cdot \left( \dfrac{1}{1 + e^x} \right)$

$\dfrac{d^2 x}{dy^2} = \dfrac{-e^x}{(1 + e^x)^3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{-e^x}{(1 + e^x)^3}$

questions.solution:
For the function $f(x) = e^{\sqrt{5x - 3 - 2x^2}}$ to be defined, the expression inside the square root must be non-negative.

$5x - 3 - 2x^2 \ge 0$

$2x^2 - 5x + 3 \le 0$

$2x(x - 1) - 3(x - 1) \le 0$

$1 \le x \le \dfrac{3}{2}$

questions.q:
$\displaystyle\int e^{2x} \dfrac{2(\sin 2x \cos 2x - 1)}{2 \sin^2 2x} \, dx = A \, e^{2x} \cot 2x + c$
(Where c is the constant of integration.), then $A^3 =$
questions.solution:
Let the given integral be $I$.

$I = \int e^{2x} \dfrac{2(\sin 2x \cos 2x - 1)}{2 \sin^2 2x} \, dx$

$I = \int e^{2x} \left( \dfrac{\sin 2x \cos 2x}{\sin^2 2x} - \dfrac{1}{\sin^2 2x} \right) \, dx$

$I = \int e^{2x} (\cot 2x - \csc^2 2x) \, dx$

We know the standard integral form: $\int e^{ax} (a f(x) + f'(x)) \, dx = e^{ax} f(x) + c$.

Let $a = 2$ and $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{2} \cot 2x$.

Then $a f(x) = 2 \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \cot 2x \right) = \cot 2x$.

Differentiating $f(x)$ with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{2} (-\csc^2 2x) \times 2 = -\csc^2 2x$

Substituting these into the integral, we get:

$I = \int e^{2x} (2 f(x) + f'(x)) \, dx = e^{2x} f(x) + c$

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} e^{2x} \cot 2x + c$

Comparing this with the given expression $A \, e^{2x} \cot 2x + c$, we find:

$A = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Therefore, $A^3 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3 = \dfrac{1}{8}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{8}$

questions.q: If $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\sin 2x}{\sin^4 x + \cos^4 x} \, dx = f(x) + c$ where c is constant of integration, then the value of $\tan(f(x))$ is
questions.solution:
The given integral is $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\sin 2x}{\sin^4 x + \cos^4 x} \, dx$.

Dividing the numerator and the denominator by $\cos^4 x$, we get

$\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\dfrac{2\sin x \cos x}{\cos^4 x}}{\dfrac{\sin^4 x + \cos^4 x}{\cos^4 x}} \, dx$

$= \displaystyle\int \dfrac{2\tan x \sec^2 x}{\tan^4 x + 1} \, dx$

Substituting $\tan^2 x = t$, we get $2\tan x \sec^2 x \, dx = dt$.

The integral becomes

$\displaystyle\int \dfrac{dt}{t^2 + 1} = \tan^{-1}(t) + c$

Substituting back $t = \tan^2 x$, we get

$f(x) + c = \tan^{-1}(\tan^2 x) + c$

Comparing both sides, $f(x) = \tan^{-1}(\tan^2 x)$.

Therefore, $\tan(f(x)) = \tan(\tan^{-1}(\tan^2 x)) = \tan^2 x$.

Answer: $\tan^2 x$

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{30x^{14} + 15^x \log 225}{x^{15} + 15^x} \, dx =$
options: $x^{15} + 15x^{14} + 30x^{13} + c$, where c is the constant of integration
$\dfrac{\log(x^{15} + 15^x)}{2} + c$, where c is the constant of integration
$\log(x^{15} + 15^x)^2 + c$, where c is the constant of integration
$\log(x^{15} + 15^x) + c$, where c is the constant of integration
questions.solution:
Let $I = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{30x^{14} + 15^x \log 225}{x^{15} + 15^x} \, dx$

Let $x^{15} + 15^x = t$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, we get

$(15x^{14} + 15^x \log 15) \, dx = dt$

Multiplying by $2$, we get

$(30x^{14} + 2 \cdot 15^x \log 15) \, dx = 2 \, dt$

Since $2 \log 15 = \log(15^2) = \log 225$, this becomes

$(30x^{14} + 15^x \log 225) \, dx = 2 \, dt$

Substituting this into the integral, we obtain

$I = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{2}{t} \, dt$

$I = 2 \log t + c$

$I = \log(t^2) + c$

$I = \log(x^{15} + 15^x)^2 + c$

Answer: $\log(x^{15} + 15^x)^2 + c$, where c is the constant of integration

questions.solution:
The principal value of $\tan^{-1}(\sqrt{3})$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

The principal value of $\sec^{-1}(-2)$ is $\pi - \sec^{-1}(2) = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.

The principal value of $\sin^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ is $-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

Substituting these values into the given expression:

$\dfrac{\pi}{3} + \dfrac{2\pi}{3} - \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$

$= \pi + \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$= \dfrac{7\pi}{6}$

Answer: $\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$

questions.q: If $y = \tan^{-1}\left\{\dfrac{\sqrt{1 + x^2} - \sqrt{1 - x^2}}{\sqrt{1 + x^2} + \sqrt{1 - x^2}}\right\}$, where $|x| \lt  1$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $x^2 = \cos 2\theta$. Then $\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}(x^2)$.

Substituting this into the given expression, we get:

$\sqrt{1 + x^2} = \sqrt{1 + \cos 2\theta} = \sqrt{2\cos^2\theta} = \sqrt{2}\cos\theta$

$\sqrt{1 - x^2} = \sqrt{1 - \cos 2\theta} = \sqrt{2\sin^2\theta} = \sqrt{2}\sin\theta$

Now, substitute these into $y$:

$y = \tan^{-1}\left\{\dfrac{\sqrt{2}\cos\theta - \sqrt{2}\sin\theta}{\sqrt{2}\cos\theta + \sqrt{2}\sin\theta}\right\}$

Dividing the numerator and the denominator by $\sqrt{2}\cos\theta$:

$y = \tan^{-1}\left\{\dfrac{1 - \tan\theta}{1 + \tan\theta}\right\}$

$y = \tan^{-1}\left\{\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \theta\right)\right\}$

$y = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \theta$

Substituting back $\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}(x^2)$:

$y = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}\cos^{-1}(x^2)$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0 - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{1 - (x^2)^2}}\right) \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}(x^2)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^4}} \cdot 2x$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^4}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^4}}$

questions.q: $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\log|2 + x| - \log|2 - x|}{\tan x}\right] = $ .......
questions.solution:
As $x \to 0$, $2+x \gt 0$ and $2-x \gt 0$, so the absolute value signs can be removed:

$\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\log(2 + x) - \log(2 - x)}{\tan x}$

This limit is of the form $\dfrac{0}{0}$. Applying L'Hospital's rule by differentiating the numerator and the denominator with respect to $x$:

$\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2 + x} - \dfrac{1}{2 - x}(-1)}{\sec^2 x}$

$= \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2 + x} + \dfrac{1}{2 - x}}{\sec^2 x}$

Substituting $x = 0$:

$= \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}}{1} = 1$

Answer: $1$

questions.q: In L.P.P., the corner points of the feasible region for the constraints $3x - y \geq 6, x \leq 3, y \leq 2, y \geq 0, x \geq 0$ are .....
questions.solution:
The given constraints are $3x - y \geq 6$, $x \leq 3$, $y \leq 2$, $x \geq 0$, $y \geq 0$.

The boundary lines for the feasible region are $3x - y = 6$, $x = 3$, $y = 2$, $x = 0$, and $y = 0$.

Finding the intersection points of the line $3x - y = 6$ with the other boundary lines:
Intersection with $y = 0$: $3x - 0 = 6 \Rightarrow x = 2$. The point is $(2, 0)$.
Intersection with $y = 2$: $3x - 2 = 6 \Rightarrow 3x = 8 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{8}{3}$. The point is $\left(\dfrac{8}{3}, 2\right)$.

The other corner points are formed by the intersection of the remaining boundary lines $x = 3$, $y = 2$, and $y = 0$ that satisfy $3x - y \geq 6$:
Intersection of $x = 3$ and $y = 0$ is $(3, 0)$.
Intersection of $x = 3$ and $y = 2$ is $(3, 2)$.

Checking these points against all constraints:
For $(2, 0)$: $3(2) - 0 = 6 \geq 6$, $2 \leq 3$, $0 \leq 2$. (Satisfies all)
For $\left(\dfrac{8}{3}, 2\right)$: $3\left(\dfrac{8}{3}\right) - 2 = 6 \geq 6$, $\dfrac{8}{3} \leq 3$, $2 \leq 2$. (Satisfies all)
For $(3, 2)$: $3(3) - 2 = 7 \geq 6$, $3 \leq 3$, $2 \leq 2$. (Satisfies all)
For $(3, 0)$: $3(3) - 0 = 9 \geq 6$, $3 \leq 3$, $0 \leq 2$. (Satisfies all)

Thus, the corner points of the feasible region are $\left(\dfrac{8}{3}, 2\right), (3, 2), (3, 0), (2, 0)$.

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{8}{3}, 2\right), (3, 2), (3, 0), (2, 0)$

questions.q: The statement pattern $(p \wedge q) \rightarrow (r \vee \sim s)$ is false. Then the truth values of $p, q, r$ and $s$ are respectively
questions.solution:
The given statement pattern is $(p \wedge q) \rightarrow (r \vee \sim s)$.

An implication $A \rightarrow B$ is false if and only if $A$ is true and $B$ is false.

Therefore, $(p \wedge q)$ is true and $(r \vee \sim s)$ is false.

For $(p \wedge q)$ to be true, both $p$ and $q$ must be true. Thus, $p = \text{T}$ and $q = \text{T}$.

For $(r \vee \sim s)$ to be false, both $r$ and $\sim s$ must be false. Thus, $r = \text{F}$ and $\sim s = \text{F}$.

Since $\sim s = \text{F}$, $s$ must be true, so $s = \text{T}$.

The truth values of $p, q, r$ and $s$ are T, T, F, T respectively.

Answer: T, T, F, T

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Consider the statement patterns
A. $(q \rightarrow p) \vee (p \rightarrow q)$
B. $(\sim p \vee \sim q) \leftrightarrow \sim (p \wedge q)$
C. $[(p \vee q) \wedge \sim p] \wedge \sim q$
D. $(p \wedge q) \wedge (\sim p \vee \sim q)$
then statement patterns
options: A and B are contradictions, C and D are tautologies.
A and B are tautologies, C and D are contradictions.
A, B, C, D all are tautologies.
A, B, C, D all are contradictions.
questions.solution:
For statement pattern A:
$(q \rightarrow p) \vee (p \rightarrow q) \equiv (\sim q \vee p) \vee (\sim p \vee q) \equiv (\sim q \vee q) \vee (\sim p \vee p) \equiv T \vee T \equiv T$
Thus, A is a tautology.

For statement pattern B:
By De Morgan's Law, $\sim (p \wedge q) \equiv \sim p \vee \sim q$.
The statement becomes $(\sim p \vee \sim q) \leftrightarrow (\sim p \vee \sim q)$, which is of the form $X \leftrightarrow X \equiv T$.
Thus, B is a tautology.

For statement pattern C:
$[(p \vee q) \wedge \sim p] \wedge \sim q \equiv [(p \wedge \sim p) \vee (q \wedge \sim p)] \wedge \sim q \equiv [F \vee (q \wedge \sim p)] \wedge \sim q \equiv (q \wedge \sim p) \wedge \sim q \equiv \sim p \wedge (q \wedge \sim q) \equiv \sim p \wedge F \equiv F$
Thus, C is a contradiction.

For statement pattern D:
$(p \wedge q) \wedge (\sim p \vee \sim q) \equiv (p \wedge q) \wedge \sim (p \wedge q)$, which is of the form $X \wedge \sim X \equiv F$.
Thus, D is a contradiction.

Therefore, A and B are tautologies, while C and D are contradictions.

Answer: A and B are tautologies, C and D are contradictions.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}_{3 \times 3}$, and $A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \gamma & -1 & 1 \\ \alpha & 6 & -5 \\ \beta & -2 & 2 \end{bmatrix}_{3 \times 3}$, then $|\alpha \cdot \beta \cdot \gamma| = $ _____ (where $|\cdot|$ denotes the absolute value)
questions.solution:
The determinant of matrix $A$ is:

$|A| = 2(1 \times 3 - 0 \times 1) - 0 + (-1)(5 \times 1 - 1 \times 0) = 6 - 5 = 1$

Since $|A| = 1$, the inverse of $A$ is simply its adjugate matrix, $A^{-1} = \text{adj}(A)$.

The elements $\gamma, \alpha, \beta$ form the first column of $A^{-1}$, which corresponds to the cofactors $C_{11}, C_{12}, C_{13}$ of the first row of matrix $A$.

Calculating these cofactors:

$C_{11} = (1)(3) - (0)(1) = 3 \Rightarrow \gamma = 3$

$C_{12} = -((5)(3) - (0)(0)) = -15 \Rightarrow \alpha = -15$

$C_{13} = (5)(1) - (1)(0) = 5 \Rightarrow \beta = 5$

The product of these values is:

$\alpha \cdot \beta \cdot \gamma = (-15) \cdot 5 \cdot 3 = -225$

Taking the absolute value:

$|\alpha \cdot \beta \cdot \gamma| = |-225| = 225$

Answer: $225$

questions.q: The joint equation of the pair of lines through the origin and making an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ with the line $3x + y - 6 = 0$ is
questions.solution:
Slope of the given line $3x + y - 6 = 0$ is $m_1 = -3$.

Let $m$ be the slope of a line passing through the origin and making an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ with the given line.

Using the angle formula, $\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \left| \dfrac{m - m_1}{1 + m m_1} \right|$

$1 = \left| \dfrac{m - (-3)}{1 + m(-3)} \right| = \left| \dfrac{m + 3}{1 - 3m} \right|$

Squaring both sides, we get:

$(1 - 3m)^2 = (m + 3)^2$

$1 - 6m + 9m^2 = m^2 + 6m + 9$

$8m^2 - 12m - 8 = 0$

Dividing by $4$, we get $2m^2 - 3m - 2 = 0$.

Since the lines pass through the origin, their equations are of the form $y = mx$, which implies $m = \dfrac{y}{x}$.

Substituting $m = \dfrac{y}{x}$ in the quadratic equation:

$2\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)^2 - 3\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) - 2 = 0$

$2y^2 - 3xy - 2x^2 = 0$

Multiplying by $-1$, we obtain the joint equation:

$2x^2 + 3xy - 2y^2 = 0$.

Answer: $2x^2 + 3xy - 2y^2 = 0$

questions.q: The area of the triangle formed by the lines joining the vertex of the parabola $x^2 = 48y$ to the ends of its latus rectum, is .....
questions.solution:
The given equation of the parabola is $x^2 = 48y$.

Comparing this with the standard form $x^2 = 4ay$, we get $4a = 48$, which gives $a = 12$.

The vertex of the parabola is $O(0, 0)$.

The ends of the latus rectum for $x^2 = 4ay$ are $(2a, a)$ and $(-2a, a)$.

Substituting $a = 12$, the ends of the latus rectum are $L(24, 12)$ and $L'(-24, 12)$.

The area of the triangle formed by the vertex and the ends of the latus rectum is given by $\dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$.

The base is the length of the latus rectum $LL' = 4a = 48$.

The height is the distance from the vertex to the latus rectum, which is $a = 12$.

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 48 \times 12 = 288$ sq. units.

Answer: $288$ sq. units

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A point on the parabola $y^2 = \dfrac{36}{5}x$ at which the ordinate increases at thrice the rate of the abscissa is .....
questions.solution:
Given the equation of the parabola:

$y^2 = \dfrac{36}{5}x$

Differentiating both sides with respect to time $t$:

$2y \dfrac{dy}{dt} = \dfrac{36}{5} \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

It is given that the ordinate increases at thrice the rate of the abscissa, so:

$\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 3 \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

Substituting this into the differentiated equation:

$2y \left(3 \dfrac{dx}{dt}\right) = \dfrac{36}{5} \dfrac{dx}{dt}$

$6y = \dfrac{36}{5}$

$y = \dfrac{6}{5}$

Substituting $y = \dfrac{6}{5}$ into the equation of the parabola to find $x$:

$\left(\dfrac{6}{5}\right)^2 = \dfrac{36}{5}x$

$\dfrac{36}{25} = \dfrac{36}{5}x$

$x = \dfrac{1}{5}$

The required point is $\left(\dfrac{1}{5}, \dfrac{6}{5}\right)$.

questions.q: The number of cubic equations that can be formed with the coefficients 0, 3, 2, 4, 5, 6 when repetition of coefficients is allowed, is....
questions.solution:
A cubic equation is of the form $ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d = 0$, where $a \neq 0$.

The given set of coefficients is $\{0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$, which contains 6 elements.

Since $a \neq 0$, the coefficient $a$ can be chosen in 5 ways (any number from the set except 0).

The coefficients $b, c,$ and $d$ can each be chosen in 6 ways, as repetition of coefficients is allowed.

Total number of cubic equations $= 5 \times 6 \times 6 \times 6 = 1080$.

Answer: $1080$

questions.q: Let $X \sim B\left(6, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$. Then the maximum probability occurs at
questions.solution:
Given $X \sim B\left(6, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$, the probability mass function is given by

$P(X = x) = ^{6}C_{x} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x} \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{6-x} = ^{6}C_{x} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{6}$

To maximize $P(X = x)$, the binomial coefficient $^{6}C_{x}$ must be maximum.

For an even integer $n$, the maximum value of $^{n}C_{x}$ occurs at $x = \dfrac{n}{2}$.

Here $n = 6$, so the maximum value occurs at $x = \dfrac{6}{2} = 3$.

Thus, the maximum probability occurs at $X = 3$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A random variable X takes the values 0, 1, 2, 3 and its mean is $1.3$. If $P(X=3) = 2P(X=1)$ and $P(X=2) = 0.3$, then $P(X=0)$ is
questions.solution:
Let $P(X=1) = p$ and $P(X=0) = q$.

Given $P(X=3) = 2P(X=1) = 2p$ and $P(X=2) = 0.3$.

The sum of all probabilities is $1$:

$P(X=0) + P(X=1) + P(X=2) + P(X=3) = 1$

$q + p + 0.3 + 2p = 1$

$q + 3p = 0.7$

The mean of the random variable is given as $1.3$:

$\sum x_i P(x_i) = 1.3$

$0(q) + 1(p) + 2(0.3) + 3(2p) = 1.3$

$p + 0.6 + 6p = 1.3$

$7p = 0.7 \Rightarrow p = 0.1$

Substituting the value of $p$ in the first equation:

$q + 3(0.1) = 0.7$

$q = 0.4$

Thus, $P(X=0) = 0.4$.

Answer: $0.4$
